verdict.rationale: Groq's docs position the product as fast LLM inference, with service tiers to tune for latency and throughput, a Flex tier for high-throughput workloads, and streaming for real-time output. Hands-on HN reports measure 450–490+ tokens/sec, and Groq staff describe low-latency, queue-free serving with good throughput even at batch size 1. Missing for 10: first-party or independent time-to-first-token measurements, since the evidence quantifies throughput but not TTFT directly.

support.subject: As a developer, I can serve latency-sensitive workloads with fast time-to-first-token and high-throughput generation

citations.quote: Groq offers multiple service tiers so you can tune for latency, throughput, and reliability.
Flex Processing is a service tier optimized for high-throughput workloads that prioritizes fast inference
you can stream the model's response in real-time. This allows your application to display the response as it's being generated
I'm achieving consistent 450+ tokens/sec for Mixtral 8x7b 32k and ~200 tps for Llama 2 70B-4k.
our LPU architecture allows us to deliver good throughput even at batch size 1.
